data.narrative:
CubeFabs is a Series E semiconductors company founded by Matthew Putman (PhD, former Columbia materials science professor) and his father John Putman. The target has raised approximately $182M to date. The broader Chips & Semiconductors sector includes 11 peer companies (3 public: ALAB, NVDA, AMD; 8 private including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and Etched), though same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within this space remain limited for narrow peer-set analysis.

Valuation triangulation relies on a single applicable method: stage-progression analysis. Using the $182M total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.4x step-up multiplier typical of Series E to subsequent-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $255M. This method assumes normalized step-up momentum consistent with frontier-hardware venture financings. Public semiconductor comparables (median P/S of 21.4x across ALAB, NVDA, AMD) cannot be applied without CubeFabs' revenue, which remains undisclosed.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $217M to $293M, centered on $255M, though this reflects a single methodological anchor. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficiently granular private-company comparables at Series E stage in semiconductors, lack of disclosed revenue for CubeFabs, and unknown trajectory of capital deployment efficiency relative to sector peers. Any revision should await either comparable financings in frontier chip hardware or disclosure of revenue metrics.
